newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa rise halted by origin selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa rise halted by origin selling.

text.p: London cocoa futures firmed up on Thursday but a renewed attempt to test higher ground was thwarted by Ivorian shippers who sold the market, trade sources said.

The rally was led by trade and industry buying but stalled at 887 stg basis March, disappointing a few bulls that were hoping for a more energetic push to test resistance at 890 stg and more importantly above 900.
"In the end people will want to buy this market. But every time it rallies it resumes the downtrend again and comes lower than the previous low," said one trader.
The common view is that funds, which hold the key for upside gains and are believed to be sitting on shorts, are unlikely to be even tempted to cover unless the market stages a rally above 900.
"It's looking a very convincing bear market," commented one.
March cocoa finished morning dealings three stg higher at 883 stg a tonne. Further forward contracts, especially the distant July, racked up larger gains of up to 13 stg.
Midsession volume reached 2,570 lots and AAs on March.

One trader said some speculators were dabbling in cocoa to take advantage of currency fluctuations especially after weak UK inflation data on Thursday soothed fears of a hike in interest rates that could have fuelled sterling.
The U.S. fourth quarter grind data is due to be released on Friday and analysts are expecting a small rise.
Technical analysts were sceptical of the market's ability to challenge nearby resistance just yet.
"We've got to clear 906 to say we are going further forward, but at the moment there isn't that much chance of getting there," said Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis. "It has capacity for further drift."
